# orders-api configuration

Generated by docuconf from the configuration contract of `orders-api`, exported by `docuconf-go` `0.1.0` (go). Do not edit this file: change the app's declaration, export the contract again, then run `docuconf docs`.

`orders-api` reads 7 environment variables and 2 files. 1 is required, and 3 are secret.

## Contents

**[Environment variables](#environment-variables)**

- [`ALLOWED_ORIGINS`](#allowed_origins): Origins allowed to call the API from a browser
- [`DATABASE_URL`](#database_url): Postgres connection string for the orders database (required, secret)
- [`LOG_LEVEL`](#log_level): Minimum log level emitted
- [`PORT`](#port): HTTP listen port
- [`REQUEST_TIMEOUT`](#request_timeout): Time limit for handling one request
- [`WEBHOOK_KEYS`](#webhook_keys): Keys that verify the signature on incoming payment webhooks (secret)
- [`WORKER_COUNT`](#worker_count): Number of background workers processing orders

**[Files](#files)**

- [`discounts`](#discounts): Discount codes accepted at checkout
- [`serving-tls`](#serving-tls): Certificate to serve HTTPS with. Without it, the service serves HTTP (secret)

### `WEBHOOK_KEYS`

Keys that verify the signature on incoming payment webhooks

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | `list` (list of strings) |
| Required | no |
| Secret | yes: never write its value in code, docs or a values file |
| Constraints | between 1 and 2 items; each item between 32 and 256 characters (Unicode code points) |
| Wire format | the items joined by `,` with nothing around it, such as `a,b` |
| In a values file | a `secretKeyRef` or `injected` reference, never the value |
| Sources | `secretKeyRef`, `injected` |
| Boot errors | `invalid_type`, `out_of_range`, `too_few_items`, `too_many_items` |

A webhook is accepted when it is signed with any key in the list, so the key can be rotated without turning webhooks away. To rotate:

 1. add the new key as the second item, and roll out;
 2. switch the sender to the new key;
 3. remove the old key, and roll out.

Each key is 32 to 256 characters, so an empty or truncated key fails at boot. Without this variable, the service rejects every webhook.

### `WORKER_COUNT`

Number of background workers processing orders

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | `int` (integer) |
| Required | no |
| Secret | no |
| Default | `4` |
| Constraints | between 1 and 64 |
| Wire format | a base-10 integer with no leading `+` or zeros, such as `8080` |
| In a values file | an integer |
| Sources | `literal`, `configMapKeyRef`, `resourceFieldRef`, `injected` |
| Boot errors | `invalid_type`, `out_of_range` |

Each worker holds one database connection, so keep it below the database's connection limit divided by the number of replicas. Raise it when the order queue grows faster than it drains.

## Files

The platform mounts each file at its path; the app reads it there. With `DOCUCONF_FILE_ROOT=./dev`, the SDK reads every path under `./dev` instead, for local runs.

| Property | Value |

| Type | `tls` (TLS key pair) |
| Required | no |
| Secret | yes: never write its value in code, docs or a values file |

## Sources

Where the platform may get each input from, as named in the tables above. A secret comes only from a secret store or an injector.

- `literal`: a literal value in the platform's values file
- `injected`: supplied when the container starts by an injector (`injected`), such as Bank-Vaults, `op run` or the Vault Agent injector; checked at boot
- `secretKeyRef`: a key of a Kubernetes Secret (`secretKeyRef`)
- `configMapKeyRef`: a key of a ConfigMap (`configMapKeyRef`), checked at boot
- `resourceFieldRef`: a container resource limit or request (`resourceFieldRef`), such as `limits.memory`
- `inline`: content in the platform repository (`inline`), rendered as a content-hashed ConfigMap
- `configMap`: a ConfigMap (`configMap`), one key per file
- `secret`: a Kubernetes Secret (`secret`), one key per file
- `csi`: the Secrets Store CSI driver (`csi`)
- `image`: an OCI image volume (`image`), for content too large for a ConfigMap
- `certificate`: a cert-manager Certificate (`certificate`)

## Boot errors

At boot the SDK checks every input and reports all problems together, one line each, with one of these codes. Secret values never appear in the messages.

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `missing_required` | A required input is not set, and has no default. | Set it through one of its allowed sources. |
| `invalid_type` | The value does not parse as the input's type in its wire format, or a secret still holds an unresolved injector reference (`vault:`, `op://`, `ref+`). | Write the value in the input's wire format. For an injected secret, make sure the injector runs. |
| `out_of_range` | A number, duration, length or list item is outside the input's bounds. | Use a value within the input's constraints. |
| `not_in_enum` | The value is not one of the allowed values. | Use one of the listed values, spelled exactly as listed. |
| `invalid_scheme` | The URL's scheme is not one of the allowed schemes. | Use a URL with an allowed scheme. |
| `too_few_items` | The list has fewer items than its minimum. | Add items. |
| `too_many_items` | The list has more items than its maximum. | Remove items. |
| `file_unreadable` | The file exists but cannot be read. | Check the mount, the file mode and the user the app runs as. |
| `file_malformed` | The file does not parse in its format, is a directory, is not UTF-8 text, or holds too few certificates. | Fix the content so it parses in the declared format. |
| `schema_mismatch` | The value or file parses, but does not match its JSON Schema. | Fix the content to match the schema; `docuconf vet` checks inline content before deploy. |
| `certificate_invalid` | A certificate does not parse, has expired or is not yet valid, uses a key algorithm that is not allowed, or does not chain to `ca.crt`. | Issue a valid certificate that meets the input's constraints. |
| `certificate_expiring` | The certificate has less validity left than `minRemaining`. | Renew it earlier: with cert-manager, set `renewBefore` to at least `minRemaining`. |
| `certificate_name_mismatch` | The certificate does not cover every name in `dnsNames`. | Reissue it with every name as a subject alternative name. |
| `key_mismatch` | `tls.key` does not match the certificate in `tls.crt`. | Supply the key and certificate from the same issuance. |
